transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Democrats and Republicans are spending heavily in dozens of house races between now and election
day next week.
And NPR analysis finds 70 districts where both parties are investing six-figure sums
in advertising.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports.
Reading data from Ad Impact suggests the question is less about whether there will be a Democratic
wave in the House, but rather how high it could crest.
Several races will see more than $10 million in ads between now and Tuesday, including
toss-up races in Michigan, North Carolina, New York, and Florida; seven-figure ad buys
in very conservative communities in Tennessee, Oklahoma, and Arkansas; and last-minute resources
to districts where gerrymandering by Republicans could backfire.
These 70 districts voted for Trump by an average of nine points in 2024, highlighting the impact
of the Trump administration's unpopularity with voters over the last year.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Atlanta.
Faculty at Cornell University are a step closer to taking a no-confidence vote against the
school's leadership.
It stems from the university's handling of sexual assault allegations made by a former
student in a lawsuit.
Member Station WSKG, Jeong-Yoon Han, has more.
Calls for a no-confidence vote have been mounting at Cornell after a former student, known as
Jane Doe, claimed she was gang-raped at a fraternity house in 2024.
While some faculty attempted to delay the vote against Cornell's president, that effort
failed during a heated and divisive meeting on Wednesday.
Mike Thompson, a professor at the university, called the no-confidence resolution "meaningless."
Thompson and other suggested faculty wait until an independent investigation provides
new information.
But proponents of the measure say it signals solidarity with sexual assault survivors.
Faculty at Cornell will have one week to vote on the resolution.
For NPR News, I'm Jeong-Yoon Han in Ithaca.
A down payment can be one of the biggest hurdles to purchasing a home.
NPR's Windsor Johnston reports a new study finds saving enough can take years, with wide
differences across states.
A new study from Cinch Home Services estimates nearly three years nationally to save a 15%
down payment.
Hawaii has the longest wait, at about five years.
Iowa has the shortest, around a year and nine months.
Jess Fields, the company's chief commercial officer, says the national estimate assumes
that potential buyers are saving about $1,700 per month.
Let's just say someone can only save $300 a month, it would take them about 15 years
to reach that down payment amount.
At $500 a month, it would still take over nine years to get to that goal.
And if home prices go up while buyers are saving, coming up with enough for a down payment
could take even longer.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
The head of the European Central Bank says she will soon step down.
Christine Lagarde will leave the bank early on February 7th.
That's about eight months early.
But European Central Bank officials will have time to pick her successor, and that will
come ahead of elections in Lagarde's home country, France.
A far-right conservative is leading in polls, but Lagarde has said she is not a presidential
candidate.
Elon Musk's company, Neuralink, is reporting early results for a trial of its brain implant.
NPR's Ping Huang reports this is focused on helping people with speech difficulties.
ALS, also known as Lou Gehrig's disease, is a neurological disorder.
Patients lose their ability to speak and move.
Over the past year, in the so-called voice trial, three patients with ALS received Neuralink
implants, which pick up brain signals to get processed into sound, words, and sentences.
Dr. Nader Paradian, at UT Southwestern, is principal investigator.
He hopes to apply it more broadly, which means recruiting more patients with other diagnoses
so we can learn more about how it's the same or how it might be different and how we might
have to customize it for those different populations, such as those who have had spinal cord injuries
or stroke.
Paradian says they're still working on the implant's ability to discern thoughts a patient
wants to share from those they do not.
The results presented at an ALS conference have not yet been peer reviewed.
Ping Huang, NPR News.
The Milwaukee Brewers are this year's World Series champions.
They beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 last night in Florida.
You're listening to NPR News.

topics.text: Democrats and Republicans spending heavily in 70 House districts with six-figure ad buys before next week's election
Cornell University faculty move closer to no-confidence vote against leadership over handling of sexual assault allegations
Study finds saving a 15% home down payment takes nearly three years nationally, ranging from one year nine months in Iowa to five years in Hawaii
European Central Bank head Christine Lagarde to step down early on February 7th, about eight months ahead of schedule
Elon Musk's Neuralink reports early results from brain implant trial aimed at helping ALS patients speak
Milwaukee Brewers win World Series, beating Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Florida
